author: t.wambsgans
content: leanVM [0.17.0](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/853) published: removed the sidecar, back with FFI (also added C# bindings). I hope everything works fine, will test more tomorrow.

author: t.wambsgans
content: There is still more juice to be squeezed, in particular for the 16->1 recursion benchmark, we are very close to cross a power of two in the PCS (some stuff inside the STARK) that would give another 15%. We can get it by tweaking the STARK a bit, but since it would add some [complexity](https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanVM/pull/855), I have delayed for now. Because in the real world, the 16 aggregates will not arrive at the same time, and so the proposer will likely stream-prove. And thus I don't want to overengineer for a specific config that will not happen in practice.

author: potuz
content: If we go with delayed inclusion it's likely that the proposer does aggregate 16:1 not in a streamed manner. At slot N you get aggregates. You know that you're proposing at N+2 but you won't know your branch until N+1. In the happy finalizing path it's fine to be proving as soon as the aggregates for N  arrive. But in the forked case I think proposers will wait at least until all aggregates from N arrived to choose the head branch and only start aggregating then, likely during N+1, when all aggregates for N have already arrived
